You're not seeing the big picture. Imagine every app with a Google library is basically the app & mini Google Play Services. --- App & mini Google Play Services = access is restricted, like other regular apps. App & mini Google Play Services + Sandboxed Google Play (unprivileged) = virtually the same access as above App & mini Google Play Services + microG (privileged) = Google has the same access as the situations above, but with worse app compatibility, worse security (especially because of privileged access), and worse privacy (leaks). --- You're worried about apps without special permissions to anything sharing usage data that they have access to anyway while ignoring the huge problems with microG just because "Google bad". That's hardly a sane approach to privacy.
